thread:
olivia (Design): Quick follow-up from the design review: smoothing default looks visually nice but it's masking short, high-impact spikes. multiple ops testers missed 10-30s blips. we need a light-weight control, not a global change.

sam (PM): Strongly agree. Request: per-panel toggle that "preserves quick peaks" with a small marker and minimal legend footprint.

kai (Viz Eng): I prototyped `preserve_quick_peaks` using MAD + prominence. Config example:
```
preserve_mode: quick_peaks
prominence_factor: 2.6
max_markers: 6
marker_shape: diamond
```
Keeps timeline clean but surfaces short spikes on latency and error metrics.

nora (A11y): Accessibility: preserved markers must be keyboard-focusable and expose `aria-label` like "peak +120ms at 14:03 UTC". don't rely on color: add shape + pattern for colorblind palettes. contrast check fails on dark theme with current orange.

olivia (Design): Copy for toggle: "Keep short spikes". Legend microcopy: show a tiny badge `spikes` only when a preserved spike exists; hide otherwise. keep detailed settings behind chevron.

sam (PM): Thresholds need to be metric-aware (percent vs absolute). default to `auto` but allow manual override per-panel. add telemetry for preserved-spikes-per-panel to tune heuristics.

kai (Viz Eng): Implementation notes: two-line compact legend (name + microstate) avoids overflow. performance: cap markers and prefer canvas rendering for markers to reduce DOM load. add debug overlay for QA to show preserved indices.

nora (A11y): Keyboard shortcut: Press `P` to toggle preserve for focused chart, show tooltip "P: toggle preserve spikes". ensure focus ring meets WCAG and screen reader announces state change.

ui-bot: Mock uploaded: https://redwood.design/mockups/keep_short_spikes_v1.png

olivia (Design): I'll update the component spec (copy, micro-legend behavior, responsive rules) and open a PR with QA checklist: keyboard nav, screen reader labels, color contrast, legend truncation, metric-adaptive thresholds, and marker cap stress tests.
